faq.a: Marble forms when limestone is heated and squeezed deep underground. Its calcite grains regrow into bigger interlocking crystals, which gives marble its sparkle and lets it be carved and polished.
asks: What rock does marble come from?

faq.q: Why does slate split into sheets?
faq.a: When shale is squeezed, its flat clay minerals grow and line up at right angles to the push. The rock then splits easily along those lines, which is why slate makes good roof tiles.
asks: Why is slate used for roofs?

faq.q: What is the difference between metamorphic and igneous rock?
faq.a: Igneous rock forms from melted rock that cools. Metamorphic rock is changed by heat and pressure while it stays solid.

faq.q: What happens if metamorphic rock gets hotter?
faq.a: If it gets hot enough, it partly melts and becomes magma, which can cool into igneous rock, continuing the rock cycle.
Often in the cores of old mountain ranges, where rock was buried and squeezed when continents collided, and around magma chambers, where rock was baked.

facts: Marble forms from limestone, slate from shale, and quartzite from sandstone.
The Taj Mahal is built of white marble.
